subject: Post-call: tailored eval plan & scoring rubric for Verity Labs — next steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Amira Khan <amira.khan@verity-labs.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@verity-labs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17 09:12 PST
Subject: Post-call: tailored eval plan & scoring rubric for Verity Labs — next steps

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — appreciated the clear breakdown of the two primary use cases (clinical triage summaries + research literature extraction). Quick recap and next steps so we keep momentum: 

Action items we agreed on:
- Verity: share a 1–2k row sample (CSV) with source text + desired label columns (we only need a small labeled subset to seed scoring). Prefer S3 link.
- Redwood: provide concise model recommendations, a scaffolded scoring rubric, and an initial eval run command that Verity ops can try on a short sample.
- Both: agree on success criteria (precision thresholds, latency budget) by end of next week.

Initial recommendations (high-level):
- Start with two model families: a 13B-class instruction-tuned open model (good for accuracy) + a cost-optimized 7B quantized candidate for throughput checks.
- We'll run parallel benchmark suites: accuracy (micro/macro F1), hallucination checks (fact-consistency sampler), and runtime SLO tests at 512 token context.

Attachments I uploaded for reference: redwood-model-recs.pdf (shortlist + perf expectations). Also sharing a Drive folder with benchmark templates and scorer code.

Questions for you to confirm in reply:
1) Can you share the S3 path and a short sample of the CSV schema by EOD tomorrow?
2) Any constraints on uploading sample data to our secure eval bucket (HIPAA/PII redaction needed)?

If that all sounds right I'll hand off to Ben/Marissa to outline the scoring rubric and a runnable eval command.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Amira Khan <amira.khan@verity-labs.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17 11:03 PST
Subject: Re: Post-call: tailored eval plan & scoring rubric for Verity Labs — next steps

Hi Logan — thanks for the recap. Confirming a couple things:

- We'll upload a 1.2k row sample to an internal S3 path today: s3://verity-prod-samples/annotated_subset_v1.csv. The file includes columns: id, source_text, target_summary, label_confidence, created_at.
- We do have PHI in some of the rows. We prefer that you run the evaluation in Redwood Private or our dedicated secure eval bucket; we can provide temporary IAM credentials restricted to a single prefix.
- Timeline: target to have an initial scoring report by the end of next week (Nov 24).

Also looping Noah (data engineering) who will share the S3 link and short README with the schema.

Thanks,
Amira
Head of Product, Verity Labs
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Amira Khan <amira.khan@verity-labs.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17 15:20 PST
Subject: Re: Post-call: tailored eval plan & scoring rubric for Verity Labs — next steps

Great — thanks Amira. Quick notes from the scoring / model side: 

1) Model shortlist (for initial run):
   - Llama-2-13b-instruct (float16) — baseline accuracy reference
   - Mistral-Instruct-7B (8-bit quant) — latency/cost candidate
   - Falcon-180B-maybe (we'll skip heavier ones unless you need SOTA)

2) Evaluation harness: we'll run three passes:
   - Label-match scoring (micro/macro F1 on target_summary tokens / normalized text).
   - Hallucination probe (reference-based consistency check + targeted QA prompts).
   - Latency/throughput sweep (1, 8, 16 concurrency at 512 tokens).

3) Scoring thresholds to validate:
   - Minimum: micro-F1 >= 0.72 on the labeled subset.
   - Hallucination rate <= 4% on the probe set.
   - P95 latency <= 220ms on our 7B quant candidate for the target concurrency (we'll report these relative to your dataset once run).

4) Cost note: expect the 13B run to cost ~2–3x the quantized 7B over the same token volume. We'll include an estimated token cost with the report.

I'll attach a short scoring-rubric.md and a link to a Drive folder with the eval notebook. Also: Marissa will share the CSV template we prefer for the scorer (a simple id, input_text, expected_output, label).

Command example (high-level) to run a Redwood eval (we'll provide a ready-to-run script for your ops):

redwood eval run --dataset s3://verity-prod-samples/annotated_subset_v1.csv \\n  --models llama-2-13b-instruct,mistral-instruct-7b \\n  --scorer scoring-rubric.md \\n  --output s3://verity-prod-samples/results/verity_eval_20261117/

We'll craft a one-click script that uses temporary credentials you provide.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Amira Khan <amira.khan@verity-labs.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18 09:05 PST
Subject: Re: Post-call: tailored eval plan & scoring rubric for Verity Labs — next steps

Following up with the artifacts we discussed. Attached: verity-eval-schema.csv (CSV template) and scoring-rubric.md (detailed rubric and scorer config). A few notes on dataset formatting and scoring rules: 

- Input CSV columns (required): id, source_text, expected_summary, label_confidence, split 
  - split is train/validation/test; please mark the 1.2k sample rows as validation/test only.
- Normalization: we apply whitespace + punctuation normalization before token-level F1. The rubric includes code snippets for this.
- Partial credit: if expected_summary is a multi-sentence extraction, we score at the sentence-level and compute micro-F1 across sentences (details in scoring-rubric.md).
- Edge cases: for redacted PHI tokens we treat redaction markers as wildcard matches (documented in rubric).

Operational notes:
- If you want us to run in your Private deployment, we'll need a short maintenance window to stage the eval job and a single IAM role with get/put access to the S3 prefix.
- We can also run in Redwood Dedicated under a temporary dedicated queue (adds small queueing overhead but keeps data in Redwood-managed infra).

I'll follow up with the actual CSV and rubric attachments in a separate secure transfer (per Amira's PHI note).

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: verity-eval-schema.csv; scoring-rubric.md

- Noah will provision the S3 path and share a temporary read-only IAM role for the prefix by tomorrow morning.
- We prefer Redwood to run the eval in our Private eval bucket (PHI constraints). Please send the exact IAM role name and a short runbook for the eval so we can provision.
- Timeline: aim for an initial report by Nov 24. Can you also include a short example of the redwood eval run output we should expect (artifact filenames and basic JSON report fields)?

If you can DM or share the runbook link to my inbox I’ll get the infra folks to whitelist it.

Appreciate the fast follow-up — looking forward to the results.

— Amira
Head of Product, Verity Labs
